source: Creator killed the forced weekend-trip route and requested a fresh human, behavior-led visual rethink on 2026-07-30.
guardrail_role: engineering blocks only hard failures after the free creative pass

concept.title: More Unofficial Rules of Marriage
concept.human_truth: Marriage becomes meaningful through tiny recurring behaviors in which each person is alternately absurd, prepared, guilty, useful and present.
concept.emotional_arc: this is you -> this is me -> this is both of us -> this is why it works
concept.visual_system: An observational anthology of nine independent marriage vignettes. No forced chronology or recurring plot object.
concept.no_object_motif_reason: The public relationship mirror accumulates through changing behaviors and role reversals; forcing one recurring prop would make the independent truths feel constructed.

slides.copy:
More unofficial rules of marriage
that nobody tells you
slides.visual: A warm lived-in entryway five minutes before leaving. Aachu is seated on a low bench fastening one shoe while holding Zuv's missing wallet out toward him without looking up. Zuv stands nearby checking the wrong jacket pocket, then notices the wallet in her hand with a sheepish smile. One concise behavior introduces the marriage world: one person is already holding what the other is looking for.
slides.cta_intent: Make married viewers swipe because the opening incident already feels like their house.
slides.pose: Aachu seated in three-quarter view with her expressive face visible; Zuv standing in profile with his face readable; natural two-inch height relationship.
slides.wardrobe: Distinct leaving-home casual outfits selected from identity references.
slides.props: One wallet, two shoes, one jacket; no suitcase, phone or decorative clutter.
slides.background: Entryway bench, one wall hook and open interior doorway under warm morning practical light.
slides.continuity_lock: Exactly two people. This is an anthology cover, not the first event in a continuous day.

shot_ladder.primary_action: one searches while the other already holds the missing object

slides.copy:
Rule no. 1
“Should we order something?”
is not a question.
The decision has already been made.
slides.visual: At a small dining nook, Aachu asks with exaggerated innocence while sliding one phone toward Zuv. The food basket is already visibly full through simple dish thumbnails and a large checkout shape with no readable UI. Zuv looks from the loaded phone to her face with amused recognition; one finger is already moving toward confirmation.
slides.cta_intent: Invite viewers to send it to the partner who asks only after choosing.
slides.pose: Aachu foreground over-shoulder; Zuv's full reaction face across the small table.
slides.wardrobe: Different relaxed home clothes selected from identity references.
slides.props: Exactly one phone and two empty plates; no delivery packaging.
slides.background: Compact dining nook under soft evening pendant light.
slides.continuity_lock: Exactly two people. The phone supplies the evidence; expressions supply the joke.

shot_ladder.primary_action: a preloaded food order is presented as an open question
shot_ladder.repeated_prop_check: phone use is limited to the two evidence-dependent slides and changes function

slides.copy:
Rule no. 2
If one person asks, “Kahan hai?”
The other must find it
without being told what “it” is.
slides.visual: At a bright bedroom vanity, Zuv searches drawers with growing seriousness while his sunglasses sit plainly on top of his own hair. Aachu appears only through a clean shoulder/profile edge, silently pointing upward at his head. He follows her finger with his eyes and begins to realize.
slides.cta_intent: Make viewers instantly identify the household finder and the household searcher.
slides.pose: Zuv single-person dominant with face and sunglasses clear; Aachu is partial evidence, not a second posed figure.
slides.wardrobe: Distinct daytime casual wardrobe from identity references.
slides.props: One pair of sunglasses and one partly open drawer.
slides.background: Vanity edge and bright window light; no mirror reflection or duplicate person.
slides.continuity_lock: Exactly two actual people but only one full figure. No live-looking reflection.

shot_ladder.primary_action: searching for sunglasses already on the searcher's head

slides.copy:
Rule no. 3
Old screenshots
do not have an expiry date.
They can be presented as evidence
at any time.
slides.visual: A tight sofa-side evidence frame. Aachu's attached hand holds one phone toward Zuv; the screen shows only abstract old message blocks and a tiny non-readable date shape. Zuv's confident explaining gesture has frozen mid-air while his expression shifts into a caught, sheepish smile. Aachu's amused eye and cheek remain visible at the near edge.
slides.cta_intent: Give screenshot keepers and screenshot victims an immediate send reason.
slides.pose: Tight evidence-and-reaction composition with both faces sufficiently visible for identity.
slides.wardrobe: Different cozy evening clothes derived from identity references.
slides.props: One phone only; no readable chat text or extra UI.
slides.background: Soft sofa fabric and one lamp glow, heavily simplified.
slides.continuity_lock: Exactly two people and one phone. The reaction must dominate over the screen.

shot_ladder.primary_action: old phone evidence stops a confident defence
shot_ladder.repeated_prop_check: phone now functions as historical evidence, not food ordering

slides.copy:
Rule no. 4
The person who did not pack
will always ask,
“Charger rakh liya?”
Usually when you’re already in the cab.
slides.visual: Inside the back seat of a cab, both faces are clear in a clean medium two-shot. Zuv leans forward with one anxious questioning hand. Aachu sits beside the packed tote and silently lifts the neatly coiled charger between two fingers with a deadpan, already-handled-it expression. His anxiety collapses into sheepish relief. No home doorway or forgotten wall socket.
slides.cta_intent: Make packers send it to the partner who audits from the passenger seat.
slides.pose: Both seated naturally; Aachu owns the charger and bag; Zuv owns only the questioning gesture.
slides.wardrobe: Distinct travel-casual clothes chosen from identity references.
slides.props: One packed tote and one coiled charger.
slides.background: Soft cab upholstery and blurred street through the window; driver excluded.
slides.continuity_lock: Exactly two people, no driver or reflection. Both faces must be large enough for identity evaluation.

shot_ladder.primary_action: one asks while the other silently reveals the already-packed charger

slides.copy:
Rule no. 5
Wi-Fi starts working
the moment your spouse enters the room.
Nobody knows why.
slides.visual: Low floor-level view beside a router. Aachu sits cross-legged after failed troubleshooting, holding one loose cable and staring at the now-steady green lights with personal betrayal. Zuv has just entered the doorway carrying nothing, both hands open in a helpless shrug and face clearly visible. The laptop nearby shows one simple connected symbol, no interface.
slides.cta_intent: Recognize the spouse whose mere presence fixes devices.
slides.pose: Aachu grounded in foreground; Zuv upright in doorway; both faces readable and no body intersects architecture.
slides.wardrobe: Different lazy-home outfits from identity references.
slides.props: One router, one traceable cable and one laptop.
slides.background: Minimal study corner with clean wall and doorway planes.
slides.continuity_lock: Exactly two people. Zuv performs no causal action; timing and reaction create the joke.

shot_ladder.primary_action: connection resolves exactly as the uninvolved spouse enters

slides.copy:
Rule no. 6
Midnight hunger
is never one person’s emergency.
The entire house gets activated.
slides.visual: High overhead midnight kitchen. Aachu stands at the open refrigerator passing one ingredient backward; Zuv catches it while already setting a pan on the stove. Their bodies form one circular workflow under a single warm light pool. Two plates wait on the counter. No phone, ordering interface or delivery person.
slides.cta_intent: Make couples recognize how one person's hunger mobilizes both.
slides.pose: Both actively upright at separate stations with one clear ingredient handoff.
slides.wardrobe: Distinct tasteful night layers derived from identity references.
slides.props: One ingredient, one pan and exactly two plates.
slides.background: Dark quiet home around one warm kitchen pool; sparse causal details only.
slides.continuity_lock: Exactly two people and one clean handoff. No extra diners, flames near fabric or anonymous hands.

shot_ladder.repeated_prop_check: food returns as physical cooking, not phone ordering

slides.copy:
Rule no. 7
Every unnecessary purchase
begins immediately after
a serious conversation
about saving money.
slides.visual: Grocery-store aisle from basket height. Aachu and Zuv simultaneously lower one unnecessary item each into the same basket: she has a novelty candle, he has an absurdly large snack box. They catch each other in the act and freeze with identical guilty expressions before laughing. The basket contains only essentials underneath, making the additions readable.
slides.emotion: equal responsibility for the broken budget
slides.cta_intent: Avoid gender blame and give both partners a 'this is us' send reason.
slides.pose: Both crouch only slightly from the hips, comfortably and anatomically; faces remain front three-quarter and readable.
slides.wardrobe: Distinct public casual outfits based on identity references.
slides.props: One basket, one candle, one large unbranded snack box and two or three essentials.
slides.background: Soft aisle perspective with no shoppers, labels or readable packaging.
slides.continuity_lock: Exactly two people. Each owns one unnecessary purchase; guilt is perfectly reciprocal.

shot_ladder.primary_action: both sneak an unnecessary item into the basket simultaneously

slides.copy:
Rule no. 8
Nobody is actually in charge.
Both just keep showing up.
Usually saying, “Maine bola tha.”
slides.visual: On the living-room floor, a small flat-pack side table sits half assembled and gently crooked. Aachu holds the instruction sheet upside down while Zuv holds two clearly different screws. Both point at opposite parts for one beat, then notice the absurdity and laugh shoulder-to-shoulder. Their free hands naturally move toward the same loose tabletop to steady it together.
slides.cta_intent: Land the send/save thesis: marriage works through presence, not perfect competence.
slides.pose: Both seated comfortably on the floor with faces, hands and tabletop visible; closeness feels earned, not posed.
slides.wardrobe: Different relaxed weekend clothes from identity references.
slides.props: One half-built side table, one upside-down blank diagram sheet, two different screws and one screwdriver.
slides.background: Quiet living-room floor under warm late-afternoon window light.
slides.continuity_lock: Exactly two people. The table remains imperfect; both visibly steady it together.

shot_ladder.primary_action: conflicting instructions become a shared stabilizing action

copy.caption_recommended: Marriage is not one person having all the answers. Sometimes one finds the sunglasses. Sometimes one packs the charger. Sometimes both break the budget five minutes after promising not to. Nobody is fully in charge; both just keep showing up. Usually saying, “Maine bola tha.” Send this to your favourite emergency contact.

visual_setup: Native Instagram post carousel only, exact 1080x1440 final. Observational anthology, not a continuous plot. Each slide uses a distinct setting, wardrobe, camera grammar, primary action and prop system while preserving the same Aachu/Zuv identities. Emotional accumulation moves from one person's recognizable quirk to reciprocal role reversal, mutual action, shared guilt and an earned togetherness payoff. Use neutral warm ivory/off-white paper with visible grain, fine ink/pencil linework, transparent watercolor blooms, muted vintage palette, clean upper-middle text space and tiny top-right @a.storyof.two. No corporate metaphor, rulebook graphics, quote-card panels, background people, reflections, portraits, readable UI, invented labels, duplicate figures or recurring plot object.
